announcements.text: A cron job whose run is interrupted by an OpenCrabs daemon restart delivers its result to NO channel: boot revival resumes the turn with no job identity, run id or deliver_to, so the job output reaches nobody. Ship-chain hot-reloads make restarts frequent, so any factory relying on cron delivery is exposed.

vpn/services/gatus/config/config.yaml carries live credentials in plaintext, including SSH private-key blocks. Never grep it with a context flag (-A/-B), and never print a parsed form of it - json.dumps of a single endpoint dict renders the key field verbatim. Read the KEY NAMES only; to compare a value, hash it in place. The read discipline is necessary but not sufficient: the PRINT is the second chokepoint, and it is the one that fails when the read felt safe. A third chokepoint is any TOOL whose output path renders the file's content: a diff, a checksum-and-dump, or a guard that prints a drift diff between two key-bearing copies discloses both. Read the output path before you ship the tool, not after.

announcements.text: The Mac's CDP and SSH tunnels drop because the Mac is POWERED OFF, not because it sleeps: pmset reports sleep=0 and its only repeating power event is a 2:55AM WAKE, which cannot raise a machine that is off (Apple M4, Mac16,10). A powered-off Mac is offline on every transport, Tailscale included, so any browser task through the Mac CDP path fails for the whole window. CORRECTED 2026-10-20: the earlier 'offline since 2026-10-02T16:31:38Z and has not returned' is FALSE — the Mac came back and went dark again; tailscale on vpn read 2026-10-20T06:1xZ reports mac-mini Online=false, LastSeen=2026-10-19T17:20:00Z ('12h ago'). The backup half still holds EXACTLY: Gatus endpoint mac-backup's last SUCCESS remains 2026-10-02T00:41:14Z (14 successes in 50 retained results, newest result 2026-10-19T18:02:25Z), so no backup has completed since that instant. TWO CORRECTIONS, one now extended: (a) mac-cdp-tunnel is NOT a Mac-host probe — its target is ssh://78.17.187.4:15259, the agents host, where it curls localhost:9222, so its state is exposed to agents-host faults; it has been continuously False, newest 2026-10-20T06:10:56Z. (b) mac-tunnel is ALSO not a Mac probe — target ssh://172.18.0.1:4444, a local forward on the gatus host; it reads True (2026-10-20T06:09:56Z) and is NOT evidence the Mac is reachable. announcements.text: An unanswered notify to an ops-profile lane may be a re-push after ANY daemon restart, not a lane declining. The ops daemon restarts constantly, and every restart opens a boot-drain window that re-pushes parked rows, so a re-push is the COMMON case and a crash the minority one. Count restarts as STARTED events; a grep for 'Started|Stopped' returns their union and reads as roughly double the true count. Before reading `journalctl --user -u opencrabs-ops`, read the INSTRUMENT: root's user journal is VOLATILE and retains only ~6.5-10 h, and this unit's rows are lifecycle events that age out within hours of its start, so a window that does not cover the restart returns an EMPTY read indistinguishable from a clean one. Read `systemctl --user show opencrabs-ops -p NRestarts -p ActiveEnterTimestamp` and `journalctl --user --list-boots` FIRST, and prove the instrument live with a POSITIVE CONTROL (`journalctl --user -u oc-questions-push.service` must return rows); only if the window covers the restart is a zero a verdict. XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is NOT the discriminator. The daemon's own dated log ~/.opencrabs/profiles/ops/logs/opencrabs.YYYY-MM-DD is on disk and outlives journald. THE UNIT IS KILLED BY ITS OWN CGROUP, AND THE VICTIM IS NOT THE HOG: the recorded series is 20 ops-memcg kills, newest pair 2026-10-18T12:20:11Z, and every lane's tool child runs INSIDE this cgroup and counts against its 2 GiB — the daemon is a MINORITY of its own budget. `KillMode=process` means those children outlive the unit stop and keep holding the cgroup while the replacement boots. A `memory.events oom_kill` of 0 is a RESET counter and proves nothing; the declarations are `ActiveEnterTimestamp` and `dmesg` filtered on the RAW `oom_memcg=...opencrabs-ops.service` / `task_memcg=...opencrabs-ops.service` field, because three opencrabs units share one app.slice and that field is the only discriminator. A RESTART CAN BE A DEPLOY, AND IT RESETS THE COUNTER: the 2026-10-19T16:49:33Z start was a binary swap (installed binary mtime 2026-10-19T16:49:31.780Z, 93,886,936 B), not a kill, and NRestarts read 0 afterwards — a zero on this unit is a counter reset, never a clean life. Earlier deploy instance: 2026-10-19T02:37:55Z, e8f2e03d, run 39190058958. TWO QUANTITIES, NOT ONE: cgroup charge is NOT daemon RSS. In one read `memory.current` moved 44.07 MiB while VmRSS was byte-identical; at another the charge was 1865.41 MiB against 1095.63 MiB of daemon RSS, so 769.78 MiB of the charge is page cache and other charges. NEW 2026-10-20T06:06Z — THE SWAP CEILING IS NOW THE BINDING ONE: read on this box, memory.current 2,147,176,448 B = 99.99% of memory.max 2,148,364,800-ish (exactly 2,147,483,648), memory.peak 2,148,241,408 = 757,760 B OVER max, memory.high == memory.max == 2,147,483,648 (so the throttle band is deleted), memory.events high 5 / max 404,426 / oom 0 / oom_kill 0, 20 pids in the cgroup, 20 ops-memcg kills still the recorded total (no 8th). AND swap.peak == memory.swap.max == 2,684,354,560 B, i.e. the swap ceiling has ALREADY BEEN TOUCHED, with swap.current 2,364,538,880 B = 88.1% of it. A '95 pct with ~99 MiB of air' read describes the CGROUP, never the daemon. THE ARENA LEVER IS LIVE AND UNRESOLVED: 32 malloc arenas of exactly 65536 kB, flat across two samples 4 s apart, hold 738.03 MiB = 67.36 pct of VmRSS, and their VA is 2048.00 MiB = EXACTLY 100 pct of the 2 GiB cap. MALLOC_ARENA_MAX is an OPEN LEAD, not a fix: changing it decides whose work dies, so it stays behind the design gate.
announcements.evidence: Ledger n=1423 (20 kills with their oom_memcg lines, KillMode=process + OOMPolicy=continue, the falsified orphan-accumulation premise of n=1421); ledger n=1479 (arena two-sample plateau, cgroup figures, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX as open lead); live read 2026-10-20T06:06Z: systemctl --user show opencrabs-ops (NRestarts=0, ActiveEnterTimestamp=2026-10-19 16:49:33 UTC, MainPID=2815652, OOMScoreAdjust=100), the cgroup's memory.current/max/peak/swap.max/swap.peak/events, `dmesg | grep -c 'task_memcg=.*opencrabs-ops.service'` = 20, and ls -l /usr/local/bin/opencrabs mtime 2026-10-19T16:49:31.780825151Z.

announcements.text: The two board/ledger agreement gates are RETIRED, not red. tests/test_close_board_recorded.py and tests/test_board_intake_recorded.py assert a board/ledger close agreement, and this factory's issue board IS its ledger — ONE surface — so the two-surface predicate is INAPPLICABLE rather than failed. They were declared RED BY DESIGN at ledger n=611 and were the only REDs in the 23-gate audit. As of 2026-10-19 they are retired through the KIT'S DECLARED-ABSENT STATE, never by deletion: each reads the declared boundary from docs/ledger-invariants.json, this tree declares none, so each prints a named SKIP ('no docs/ledger-invariants.json — the boundary is a DECLARED factory parameter (#78 clause b)') and STILL RUNS EVERY PROBE — 11 on the close gate, 15 on the intake gate. HOW TO READ THEM NOW: a SKIP is the expected, correct state and is NOT a regression; but a RED from either gate IS a real defect — the retire was built so it cannot disguise a removed or broken gate. The four judgement probes are hermetic (a synthetic tree), and each gate keeps a positive control: a DECLARED boundary must still fail a bad row. The old 'RED BY DESIGN, do not file as a regression' instruction is WITHDRAWN — filing one of these as a regression is now the wrong call only if it SKIPPED; if it FAILED, file it. Owner directive 2026-10-19: 'i don't want to be asked such low level questions any more' — q27 is answered and the class (kit convention, internal mechanics) is now HQ's to decide, never the owner register's. Commits aed7c5af (gates + roles/hq.md + ledger n=1482) and 0c4952eb (prose refs). Full audit after: 24/24 gates PASS.

announcements.text: A Gatus alert page can be SILENTLY LOST: the relay on vpn forwards it over an SSH hop to the agents host's A2A gateway, and when that hop fails the receiver records delivered=false (transport_error) and the target lane is never woken. The owner's q16 ACCEPTS the loss, so no factory may treat a Gatus page as a guaranteed wake - verify the episode in the receiver's store or the ledger when the alert matters.
